extracted.intended_audience: researchers, policy analysts, and NIH policymakers studying grant funding and peer-review disparities
extracted.subtask_description: Summarize and evaluate empirical evidence on race/ethnicity gaps in probability of receiving NIH R01 awards, with attention to what applicant features were controlled for and where in the review process disparities arise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcome studied: probability of receiving a funded NIH R01 award
rubrics_metrics.description: Probability of receiving a funded NIH R01 award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary dependent variable for the study; all analyses and controls are oriented toward explaining differences in this outcome across racial/ethnic groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Degree type (PhD, MD, MD/PhD)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of the objective applicant features the study controlled for to isolate race/ethnicity effects; indicative of training and credential differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Year of highest degree
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Controls for cohort and career timing; used to account for differences in experience associated with degree year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Country of training
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Controlled to distinguish effects of domestic vs. international training on funding probability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type and prestige of training institution
rubrics_metrics.description: Type and prestige of training institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Captures institutional reputation/quality of training as a predictor of funding; included as an objective control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of prior publications
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure of research productivity; used as an objective control when estimating race effects on funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation count
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bibliometric indicator of research impact; matched via Web of Science and included to adjust for productivity/impact differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior NIH funding
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Controls for applicants' previous success with NIH, which strongly predicts future funding probability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior R01 awards
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific prior experience with the R01 mechanism controlled for as an indicator of established track record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Years since training completed
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Career stage control to adjust for seniority/experience differences across applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of prior R01 applications
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Controls for application experience and persistence, which affect funding probability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission status
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether the application is an initial submission or a revision; controlled because resubmissions have different funding dynamics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-identified race/ethnicity
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary independent variable of interest; used to estimate gaps in funding probability after controlling for objective features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Country of birth / country of training
rubrics_metrics.description: Country of birth / country of training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional demographic control to separate nativity/training-location effects from race/ethnicity effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employer type and characteristics
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Controls for institutional employer differences (e.g., research-intensive vs other employers) that influence funding chances.

rubrics_metrics.name: State / region
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Geographic control for regional variation in funding patterns and institutional distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key finding: race-based funding gaps (magnitude by group)
rubrics_metrics.description: After controlling for objective applicant features: Asian applicants 4 percentage points less likely; Black/African-American applicants 13 percentage points less likely (reduces to 10 percentage points after full controls); Hispanic applicants show a small, mostly non-significant gap.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quantifies the observed disparities and notes robustness to controls; highlights size and statistical significance of gaps by racial/ethnic group.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disparity arises earlier in review (impact scores, decision to discuss)
rubrics_metrics.description: Disparity at priority-score stage: among proposals with strong priority scores, funding was equal across races. Disparity arises earlier in the review process (impact scores, decision to discuss).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates which stages of peer review contribute to observed funding gaps — reviewers' decisions to discuss and early impact/priority scoring rather than final priority score/funding-stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH implicit quality criteria: significance, investigators, innovation, approach, environment
rubrics_metrics.description: The five NIH criteria (significance, investigators, innovation, approach, environment) — when applied by reviewers, generated systematically lower scores for Black applicants of equivalent objective qualifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The criteria themselves may be formally neutral, but their application by reviewers was biased; auditing application of each criterion is necessary to detect bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodological innovation: matching NIH internal data with external bibliometrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Matched NIH IMPAC II internal data with Web of Science bibliometric data to create a rigorously-controlled empirical study of racial disparities in NIH funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended methodological standard for studying funding disparities: link administrative award/application records with external measures of productivity/impact to control for objective applicant characteristics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implication for rubric design: audit each review criterion for racial disparities
rubrics_metrics.description: A defensible rubric would require regular auditing for race/ethnicity disparities at each criterion individually.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy recommendation derived from findings: implement routine disaggregated audits of reviewer scores on significance, approach, investigators, innovation, and environment to detect and remediate bias.
